reason: Skeletal dysplasia defines the disease. Hearing loss with auditory canal stenosis in 2/2 and ocular dysfunction annotated at 30-79% support both involved axes.
The defining congenital nasal malformation belongs to the pulmonary axis, which explicitly includes the nose.
Spastic paraplegia defines neurologic disease. Cataracts at 80-99% and structural skeletal deformities, including pes cavus in 4/5 and scoliosis in 2/5, support the involved axes.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease and extraocular skeletal myopathy define ophthalmoplegia and ptosis. Ataxia in 2/7 and occasional hearing loss do not establish additional common organ involvement.
Cardiac-layer inflammation establishes cardiovascular disease. Inflammation alone does not establish infection, autoimmunity or another qualifying immune mechanism.
Defective long-chain fatty-acid transport establishes a metabolic disorder. The sparse evidence supports neither additional organ labels nor greater confidence.
The injury is defined by spinal cord damage. Vertebral injury is not required; bladder sphincter dysfunction reflects neural damage and does not establish direct urinary-organ injury.
Opisthorchis infection primarily occupies and inflames the biliary tract, supporting hepatic and infectious_immune. Intestinal damage is not defining; cholangiocarcinoma is a separate later risk.

Intellectual disability and seizures define neurologic disease. Cataract/glaucoma in 3/6 and cleft palate in 2/6 meet the involvement threshold; small hands and feet alone do not establish skeletal dysfunction.
Add metabolic_endocrine to primary: amyloidosis is a protein metabolism/proteostasis disorder, and its metabolic mechanism remains applicable alongside bronchopulmonary localization.
